sentences: I pull the dipstick, wipe it clean, reinsert it, and then read the oil level on the marked scale.
I inspect the coolant reservoir to ensure the fluid sits between the minimum and maximum lines when the engine is cold.
I remove each spark plug, check the electrode gap with a feeler gauge, and replace them if worn.
I open the air filter housing, take out the old filter, and install a new one every twelve thousand miles.
I check the timing belt for cracks or fraying and verify that the tensioner pulley spins freely without noise.
I clean the battery terminals with a wire brush and apply a thin layer of dielectric grease to prevent corrosion.
I measure the alternator output voltage with a multimeter and confirm it stays between thirteen and fifteen volts.
I drain the radiator, flush the system with distilled water, and refill it with a fifty-fifty mix of coolant.
I inspect the exhaust manifold for cracks and tighten the bolts to the specified torque in a star pattern.
I remove the fuel injectors, clean them with an ultrasonic cleaner, and replace the O-rings before reinstalling them.
I remove the throttle body, spray it with cleaner, and wipe the interior bore until it is free of carbon.
I check the turbocharger shaft for play and verify that the wastegate actuator moves smoothly when I apply vacuum.
I inspect the engine mounts for cracks or separation and use a pry bar to check for excessive movement.
I check the serpentine belt for glazing and cracks, then verify the automatic tensioner holds the correct tension.
I remove the valve cover, scrape off the old gasket material, and apply a new gasket with sealant at the corners.
I pull the PCV valve from the valve cover and shake it to hear the internal check valve rattle.
I disconnect the oxygen sensor connector and measure the heater circuit resistance with a digital multimeter.
I remove the mass air flow sensor and clean the hot wire element with a specialized spray cleaner.
I screw the compression tester into each spark plug hole and crank the engine for several revolutions.
I watch the engine temperature gauge climb to the normal operating range and confirm the cooling fan engages.
